correctness.rationale: The exact fixed-total experiment is the sum of N independent incidence-column increments. Their means vanish, and their covariance is BB^T/n, where the edge Gram block of a run of length L has diagonal 2 and off-diagonal -1 and determinant L+1. The zero columns have positive mass uniformly for fixed k, and the endpoint and successive-difference phases force every edge phase to vanish modulo 2pi at a peak. This supplies Gaussian domination on the rescaled torus with no lattice multiplicity. Taylor expansion and dominated convergence give (1), uniformly since only finitely many run shapes occur. The constants for one edge, two touching and two disjoint are respectively (4pi lambda)^(-1/2), (2pi lambda sqrt(3))^(-1) and (4pi lambda)^(-1). Direct word counting at n=5,N=4 gives respectively 195, 64 and 61 admissible assignments out of 625, consistent with the finite marginal formulas. At criticality the O_k(n^(k-1)) tuples with touching edges contribute o(1), and mixed falling factorial moments give independent interval Poisson counts; bounded total mass on the compact interval gives tightness. The zero-count conclusion follows by testing the integer-valued mass at a half-integer cutoff. Above criticality Markov suffices; below it the covariance bounds for touching and disjoint pairs give relative variance o(1). Inspected the frozen finite checker without executing it; it does not purport to prove a limiting result.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Fixed-dimension moment results and sparse occupancy Poisson approximations do not give uniform point probabilities for every fixed edge-constraint pattern in the diverging-load fixed-total array. Standard general LLT plus factorial moments are techniques, not a located antecedent theorem stating or immediately encompassing the joint result.

value.rationale: Exact ties are a natural degeneracy of the discrete gradient, complementary to absolute variation. A single marginal suggests the cubic balance, but cannot decide concentration, clusters or the limiting locations. The fixed-total joint law and complete three-regime description make the result useful for understanding when an ordered histogram has no flat edge.
